input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the hand in the grey knit sleeve in the lower left foreground: it slowly and gently lifts the small white sake cup a little higher and tilts it slightly toward the left edge of the frame, as if about to take a happy sip; the person's face and head stay completely outside the frame and never appear. The hand keeps exactly five natural fingers and the cup keeps its shape. Everything else, including the sake bottles, the tokkuri, the sashimi, the grilled fish, the edamame and all dishes, the person in the navy plaid shirt at the right edge, the cabinet, the plants, the window and the poster, is completely still and motionless. A sunny, relaxed holiday afternoon in a Japanese tatami living room, warm natural sunlight, two old school friends enjoying chilled sake together. The sake is cold: no steam, no smoke, no haze. No faces are ever shown.
